newsitem.title: UK: Hyder to pay windfall tax out of borrowings.
newsitem.headline: Hyder to pay windfall tax out of borrowings.

text.p: British water company Hyder Plc, the owner of Welsh Water and South Wales Electricity said on Thursday it will pay its 282 million stg windfall tax liability, imposed by the recent Labour government budget, from borrowings.
The company said it will not challenge the legality of the tax and was confident it could deliver satisfactory dividend growth.
The new windfall tax imposed by Chancellor Gordon Brown in his first budget on July 2 was a one-off tax on excess profits of privatised utilities.
Brown's intention is to raise about 5.2 billion stg to finance various social welfare schemes.
Privatised water companies are expected to contribute about 1.65 billion stg towards this tax.

Hyder reassured on Thursday that its customers would not have to bear the burden of the tax and it would continue its earlier plans to implement customer rebates and its capital expenditure programme.
"Hyder's unregulated businesses continue to develop well and will increasingly contribute to long term dividend growth," the company said.
